scope: Regenerate Moon 2 Days 23–26 (continuous Days 52–55); local vault only, no website publishing.

prompts.scene: Walking the short level dry camp circuit after heel-retention adjustment, wearing both experimental bast soles and the complete dry-use outfit.
prompts.prompt:
Generate ONE fresh independent Humanity Handbook narrative illustration, wide landscape approximately 16:9. Luminous restrained earth-tone watercolor, fine selective brown contour ink, warm paper, softly dissolved margins, smooth translucent skin rather than etched marks. No lettering, labels, title, panels, montage or character-sheet layout.
REFERENCE ROLES: first image day-01.png fixes the SAME man's facial profile, nose/brow, dark wavy ear-length hair, short dark beard, natural skin tone and lean sinewy ordinary adult build, about thirty, plus narrative style. Second image character-sheet.png fixes ONLY the dated clothing's material, size, geometry and anatomical placement. Do not import sheet typography, multiple views or white studio background. No previous daily image is an input. Any third reference is equipment geometry only; ignore its plate style, labels and layout.
SETTING: fictional northern Iberian valley around 40,000 BP, early autumn, ordinary dry daylight, scattered woodland with ochre foliage and rocky open land. Natural anatomy: two hands, two legs, ordinary joints and fingers, no scars, tattoos, dense skin hatching, fashionable accessories, leather boots, full fur coat, metal, modern tools, modern furniture, modern pots or agricultural village. Keep object scale modest and action clear. No snow or visible moon.
CLOTHING DEFAULT (only override items explicitly removed below): small low shallow grey-brown rabbit-fur CROWN PAD with folded margins and loose forehead/back band, dark hair at edges, face/human ears/nape exposed. Plain fur ONLY, absolutely no animal head, rabbit ears, animal eyes, muzzle, whiskers, tail or chin strap. NARROW rusty fox-fur strip on man's anatomical LEFT shoulder only, not both shoulders. TWO SEPARATE flexible hanging golden grass screens, front header below collarbones and back across upper back, light horizontal paired retaining rows, thin loose shoulder supports, open side gap; each about half a metre wide and 60 cm long, reaching hips, not a cloth tunic, poncho or stiff lattice. Bark waist panels and small rabbit-fur pelvic pad beneath these. BOTH feet have low flat interlaced willow-bast soles, thin grass liners and simple plant-cord forefoot/heel retention, exposed toes and ankles. Keep actual grass, bark and fur visually distinct. Fox left means viewer RIGHT in a front-facing figure. The cap, shoulder strip, grass screens and footwear are separate objects.
SCENE — MOON 2 DAY 23, after both bast soles have been made and heel tie adjusted, during the short level dry walking test BEFORE the unsuccessful incline test. The fully clothed man takes a cautious small step on a genuinely LEVEL dry camp terrace, looking down to see whether the soles stay underneath his feet. Full body clearly visible in a front-left three-quarter view, both open-toed soles unobscured, same complete outfit as reference: cap, fox LEFT shoulder, front AND back grass panels, waist layers, TWO shoes. Relaxed balanced hands, not holding tools or weapons. Front panel gently bends with his stride; rear panel visible along side, with open flank. Camera low enough that small bast soles and retaining ties read clearly but no distorted huge feet. A low natural rock at the edge is a support used for fitting, not a bench; low debris shelter softly distant up the terrace. This is careful footwear testing beside camp, not a mountain hike, hunt, wet walk or triumphant trek. Quiet sunlight and soft woodland/valley background. Clothing and both shoes are the main technical subject; no extra shoe placed on ground because BOTH are worn in this moment.

SCENE — MOON 2 DAY 24, at the packing/storage stage AFTER the little bow-drill test flame has been extinguished, away from active fire. He has put the dry-use outfit back on: cap, narrow fox LEFT shoulder, separate grass FRONT/BACK screens and BOTH low bast soles. He kneels beside the existing low debris shelter's dry protected edge, thoughtfully inspecting the NEW small flattened split-willow fireboard with one socket near an edge and a V-shaped dust notch leading out of that edge. Hold it at a gentle readable angle in his hands. New kit B's other components are grouped on clean dry ground in front: ONE slender wooden spindle, ONE modest naturally curved wooden bow with plant-cord string attached at both ends, ONE palm-sized wooden bearing block, and a small dry bark dust catcher. These are the parts of ONE second kit, not five duplicated kits. No arrow, sword, antler spur, drill machine or modern matches. No lit fire, ember, flames, smoke or steam. Old kit A is stored separately out of frame. No invented cloth wrapper or bag. Low side/front three-quarter view keeps cap, flexible front screen, separate rear fringe, waist layers and both shoes readable; arms operate naturally without grass falling across hands. Subject is reproducible ignition parts being kept together, not another first-fire spectacle.

Fully clothed in complete sheet outfit including plain low cap, LEFT fox strip, separate front/back grass screens, waist layers and BOTH bast soles. One natural hand lightly examines the OUTSIDE corner fastening while the tray remains level and supported; the other rests on his knee, not in water. His grass fringe is kept clear of the rim. Front-left three-quarter view revealing shoulder placement and separate rear fringe at flank; footwear visible on dry ground. Quiet concentrated comparison of construction and containment. Soft terrace woodland background, no riverbank or wet-processing scene.

OVERRIDE CLOTHING: he is BAREFOOT and grass FRONT/BACK screens and crown pad are removed for this projectile session as written; he retains bark waist panels, small pelvic pad and NARROW fox strip on anatomical LEFT shoulder.
